title: AI Missions, Agent Identity & the Future of Voice Infrastructure — with Telnyx CEO David Casem
summary: He bootstrapped a telecom company, survived a DDoS attack by sending attackers Bitcoin every 6 minutes, and scaled to billions of minutes a month.
body_markdown:
He bootstrapped a telecom company, survived a DDoS attack by sending attackers Bitcoin every 6 minutes, and scaled to billions of minutes a month. This week he rode shotgun on Skywatch,[Bluejay](https://www.linkedin.com/company/get-bluejay/) 's car podcast.


[David Casem](https://www.linkedin.com/in/dcasem/) , co-founder & CEO of[Telnyx](https://www.linkedin.com/company/telnyx/) , hopped in the car — and we went deep on what the next era of voice AI actually looks like from someone who's been in the trenches longer than most.


The take I keep coming back to: we're moving from AI workflows to AI missions.
Not "did the agent handle the call?" but "did the agent accomplish a multi-step task over hours or days — scheduling, follow-ups, quote collection, the whole thing."


A few things that hit different from this one:


🔹 The workflow era gave us smarter IVRs. The missions era gives every person their own AI assistant.


🔹 Cost and quality aren't a trade-off anymore. The best infrastructure players are improving both simultaneously.


🔹 Culture eats strategy. Telnyx has nearly 400 people vibe-coding internal tools. The best orgs will learn to orchestrate more compute.


Oh, and yes — the DDoS story involves Dune references. You'll want to hear that one.
